housing: Broadland wraps around the north of Norwich, so much of its housing is suburban: post-war and modern estates in Sprowston, Hellesdon, Thorpe St Andrew and Taverham. Large new developments are being built in the growth area north-east of Norwich. The rural north has market towns such as Aylsham and Reepham and many villages, some within the Broads. Bungalows are common and the district is mostly owner-occupied.
checkinTips: Bungalows in the suburbs and villages: photograph loft hatches, flat-roofed extensions and garden paths.
Riverside and Broads homes around Wroxham and Acle: photograph moorings, garden edges and any signs of flooding or damp.
Rural homes off the gas network: photograph the oil tank, its gauge level and the boiler.
Septic tanks and private drainage in villages: photograph the access cover and note who is responsible for emptying.
New-build homes in the growth area north-east of Norwich: note snagging marks, shared parking and management company areas.
Older brick and flint cottages: photograph walls, beams and window frames for damp and rot.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe homes to the council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and take enforcement action.
